citation.authors: Agyemang C, Humphry RW, Bhopal R

cited_by.title: High blood pressure in Black adults

record.population: 22,723 adults in the Health Surveys for England (1,379 African-Caribbean, 21,344 White)
record.design: Secondary analysis of repeated cross-sectional surveys, age-specific blood pressure curves
record.finding: African-Caribbean blood pressure crossed above White at about 30-40 years. At 20-29 African-Caribbean men were advantaged, but not after that. African-Caribbean women had higher BMI than White women; men did not differ much. The authors advise extra vigilance in screening African-Caribbean patients from age 30 and call the mechanism "still mysterious".
record.note: Cross-sectional, so it compares different people at different ages, not the same people over time.

cited_by.title: Weight, BMI and losing weight safely

record.population: 22,723 adults in the Health Surveys for England (1,379 African-Caribbean)
record.design: Secondary analysis of cross-sectional surveys of blood pressure and BMI
record.finding: African-Caribbean women had higher BMI than white women; there was little difference in BMI in men.
record.note: Included only for the BMI pattern; this paper does not test the NHS BMI cut-offs.
